title: Introduce 'session-lite' ergonomic surface and coordinate SDK version bumps across Python/TypeScript/Go
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: teams repeatedly asked for a smaller, faster-to-adopt session API focused on low-friction streaming and retry presets. This PR adds a lightweight 'session-lite' surface to the core proto and implements ergonomic bindings in the Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, plus a coordinated version bump so downstream consumers get a single rollout. Key constraints: keep backward compatibility for full Session API, minimize runtime allocations for hot paths, and surface a small set of idiomatic helpers per language. Changes include a proto tweak (session.proto) with carefully added optional fields, three SDK language shims (py/ts/go) that map to the new fields with clear migration notes, and CI/release automation updates to publish SDK packages in lockstep. Checklist: - [x] Add session-lite proto message and backward-compatible accessor (proto/session.proto) - [x] Implement Python context-manager and typed thin wrapper (sdk/python/redwood/session_lite.py) - [x] Add TS AbortSignal-friendly stream helpers and AsyncIterable binding (sdk/typescript/src/session-lite.ts) - [x] Add Go SessionHandle with minimal allocations and context cancellation (sdk/go/sessionlite/session.go) - [x] Update docs/version matrix and SDK changelogs - [x] Bump versions: python 1.8.0, typescript 2.5.0, go v1.6.2 - [x] CI: add release-dry-run job and test matrix to ensure synchronized artifacts - [x] Run integration canary against staging runtime (canary-id: canary/sess-lite-2026-03) Migration notes: existing consumers of the full Session API are unaffected; opt-in to session-lite by calling the new factory helpers. For Python we added a context manager wrapper so common usage becomes: with SessionLite.from_env() as s: ... which automatically primes credentials and prefills KV cache hints. For TS, SessionLite exposes streamWithAbort(signal, opts) and a thin AsyncIterable shim for older code. For Go, SessionHandle provides Acquire/Release methods that are optimized for pooled use. See docs/sdks/version-matrix.md for language-specific examples and a table of behavioral differences. Rollout plan: merged to main, smoke-tested on staging, packages published to internal registry, external package releases scheduled 2026-03-11 with coordinated changelogs.

review_thread: Diego Martinez: Nice approach keeping full Session stable. Can we avoid copying the entire KV hints buffer on handoff? Suggest passing a read-only view.
Asha Kapoor: Good point — adjusted Go binding to use a byte-slice view instead of clone; added a small test to validate immutability contract.

Lina Chen: Python context manager looks clean. Please add a brief note in migration guide about exception handling semantics when the context manager closes (it should not swallow runtime exceptions).
Asha Kapoor: Added explicit doc paragraph and unit test asserting original exception propagates while cleanup still runs.
Omar Farouk: CI flaky on macos-latest for TS build; thread shows intermittent network calls to registry during integration. Resolved by pinning registry URL to internal mirror in CI matrix.
Diego Martinez: Approved after the minor CI fix and small nit about variable naming in ts helper (renamed 's' -> 'session').
